BST260 Final Project Proposal

Xinyi Wang

Source: vignettes/proposal.qmd

Dear BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026,

I plan to write two vignettes using CDC datasets introduced in BST260 and distributed with my finalproject package. The first compares typical outbreak size with the burden of the largest outbreaks. The second examines whether the jurisdictions with the highest current homicide death rates also experienced the largest recent increases.

Vignette 1 — Outbreak size in drinking water and treated recreational water

Research question. Among reported waterborne outbreaks, which exposure group has larger typical outbreaks, and in which group do the largest outbreaks account for a greater share of reported illnesses?

I will use waterborne, the package snapshot of records from the CDC National Outbreak Reporting System. I will convert the list to an outbreak-level table, keep records with water as the primary transmission mode, and compare outbreaks labeled exclusively as drinking water or treated recreational water. I will convert reported illness counts to numbers and document exclusions for mixed exposure categories and missing or invalid counts.

For each exposure group, I will report the number of outbreaks, the median and interquartile range of illnesses per outbreak, and the 90th percentile. I will also rank outbreaks by illness count and divide the combined illnesses in the largest 10% of outbreaks, rounded up to a whole outbreak, by the total reported illnesses in that group. A boxplot with a log scale for positive counts will show how the distributions differ, and I will report any zeros separately. These summaries capture different features of the data. A group can have a smaller median outbreak and still have more of its reported illnesses concentrated in a few large outbreaks.

Differences in detection and reporting may affect which outbreaks appear in the data. The comparison describes reported outbreaks, and the dataset lacks the exposed population counts needed to estimate individual illness risk.

Vignette 2 — High homicide death rates and large increases across jurisdictions

Research question. How much do the ten jurisdictions with the highest age-adjusted homicide death rates in 2024 overlap with the ten that experienced the largest increases from 2019 to 2024?

I will use cdcmurd, the package snapshot of the CDC/NCHS homicide mortality tables, which includes the 50 states and Washington, D.C. I will check for duplicate jurisdiction-year records and missing rates, pair each jurisdiction’s 2019 and 2024 observations, and calculate the change in deaths per 100,000 as the 2024 rate minus the 2019 rate.

I will summarize the distributions of the 2024 rates and the paired changes with medians and interquartile ranges. I will compare the two top-ten lists, include ties at either cutoff, and report the overlap. A labeled scatterplot of 2024 rate against change since 2019 will show jurisdictions that stand out on one or both measures. For selected jurisdictions that appear in only one group, I will plot annual rates from 2019 through 2024 to show whether the endpoint comparison reflects a sustained rise, a temporary spike, or a high rate that was already present in 2019.

I will report death counts alongside rates for highlighted jurisdictions because rates based on few deaths can fluctuate substantially. The analysis will describe changes over time without attributing them to a particular policy or event.

Both vignettes will document the data sources and cleaning decisions and present their findings and limitations on my pkgdown site.

AI use

I used ChatGPT to assess whether my proposed analyses were feasible.

Vignette 1 — Waterborne outbreaks

  • What would it mean if one exposure group had a lower median number of illnesses per reported outbreak but a higher share of illnesses attributable to its largest 10% of outbreaks?
  • If one exposure group has far fewer reported outbreaks, how sensitive is the top-10% illness share to rounding up and to a single unusually large outbreak? What simple sensitivity check could I report?
  • How should I summarize the records excluded for mixed exposure categories or for missing or invalid illness counts? What can the pattern of exclusions tell me about how to interpret the comparison?

Vignette 2 — Homicide death rates across jurisdictions

  • If I include all ties at the cutoff for either top-ten list, how should I report the size of each group and the number of jurisdictions in both?
  • Could comparing only 2019 and 2024 make a temporary spike look like a sustained increase? How could I use annual rates to show the difference for selected jurisdictions?
  • How should I present death counts alongside age-adjusted rates when a jurisdiction ranks high but has few deaths? What caveat should I give when interpreting its rank or rate change?
